20	func printPullUsage() {
21		fmt.Println(`Usage:
22	  okf pull [<bundle-id|git-url>] [flags]
23	
24	Pulls and installs an external knowledge bundle into .okf/vendor/ and updates okf.lock.
25	If no bundle is specified, restores all bundles declared in okf.lock.
26	
27	Flags:
28	  --registry <url>   Override canonical registry endpoint (default: https://registry.okf-memory.dev)
29	  --min-score <N>    Gate minimum bundle quality score (0-100; aborts installation if below)
30	  --force            Overwrite existing vendor installation if present
31	
32	Examples:
33	  okf pull
34	  okf pull nextjs-15
35	  okf pull nextjs-15 --min-score 80
36	  okf pull @peter/django-5-rules
37	  okf pull peter/django-5-rules@1.0.0
38	  okf pull github.com/acme/agent-rules@v1.0.0`)
39	}
40	
41	func cmdPull(args []string) {
42		fs := flag.NewFlagSet("pull", flag.ExitOnError)
43		registryURL := fs.String("registry", registry.DefaultRegistryURL, "Registry endpoint")
44		minScore := fs.Int("min-score", 0, "Gate minimum bundle quality score (0-100)")
45		force := fs.Bool("force", false, "Overwrite existing vendor installation")
46		fs.Usage = printPullUsage
47	
48		if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
49			os.Exit(2)
50		}
51	
52		if *minScore < 0 || *minScore > 100 {
53			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: --min-score must be an integer between 0 and 100\n")
54			exitFunc(2)
55			return
56		}
57	
58		if fs.NArg() < 1 {
59			if _, err := os.Stat("okf.lock"); os.IsNotExist(err) {
60				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Error: okf.lock not found. Specify a bundle to pull (e.g. 'okf pull <bundle-id>') or run in a workspace with an existing okf.lock.")
61				exitFunc(1)
62				return
63			}
64			runRestore(*registryURL, *force, *minScore)
65			return
66		}
67	
68		target := fs.Arg(0)
69		client := newRegistryClient(*registryURL)
70	
71		fmt.Printf("Resolving %s from %s...\n", target, client.BaseURL)
72		manifest, err := client.Resolve(target)
73		if err != nil {
74			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v\n", err)
75			exitFunc(1)
76			return
77		}
78	
79		if manifest.Version == "main" && (strings.HasPrefix(target, "github.com/") || strings.HasPrefix(target, "https://")) {
80			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: Pulling floating branch 'main'. Pin to @vX.Y.Z for reproducible builds.\n")
81		}
82	
83		// The manifest id comes from the registry: it must resolve inside .okf/vendor
84		// before anything is installed there or rolled back from there.
85		vendorDisplay := filepath.Join(".okf", "vendor", filepath.FromSlash(manifest.ID))
86		vendorDir, err := registry.ResolveVendorDir(".", manifest.ID)
87		if err != nil {
88			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: refusing to install bundle: %v\n", err)
89			exitFunc(1)
90			return
91		}
92		if _, err := os.Stat(vendorDir); err == nil && !*force {
93			fmt.Printf("Bundle %q is already installed in %s. Use --force to reinstall.\n", manifest.ID, vendorDisplay)
94			return
95		}
96	
97		fmt.Printf("Downloading %s (version: %s)...\n", manifest.ID, manifest.Version)
98		// Extract and validate in a fresh staging directory: rollback discards only
99		// what this invocation created, never an existing directory.
100		staging, err := registry.NewStaging(".")
101		if err != nil {
102			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: refusing to install bundle: %v\n", err)
103			exitFunc(1)
104			return
105		}
106		if err := client.DownloadAndExtract(manifest, staging.Dir); err != nil {
107			_ = staging.Discard()
108			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Download error: %v\n", err)
109			exitFunc(1)
110			return
111		}
112	
113		// Post-install validation: ensure installed bundle conforms to OKF v0.2 and passes quality gate
114		rollback := func() {
115			if err := staging.Discard(); err != nil {
116				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: rollback refused: %v\n", err)
117			}
118		}
119	
120		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(staging.Dir, "index.md")); os.IsNotExist(err) {
121			rollback()
122			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: bundle %q is not a valid OKF v0.2 bundle: missing index.md (installation rolled back)\n", manifest.ID)
123			exitFunc(1)
124			return
125		}
126	
127		vb, err := okf.LoadBundle(staging.Dir)
128		if err != nil {
129			rollback()
130			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: bundle %q failed to load: %v (installation rolled back)\n", manifest.ID, err)
131			exitFunc(1)
132			return
133		}
134	
135		diag := okf.Validate(vb, okf.ValidateOptions{
136			Strict:   true,
137			MinScore: *minScore,
138		})
139		if !diag.IsConformant || !diag.GatePassed {
140			rollback()
141			if *minScore > 0 && diag.Scorecard != nil && diag.Scorecard.Score < *minScore {
142				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: bundle %q failed quality gate: score %d is below required minimum %d (Grade: %s); installation rolled back\n",
143					manifest.ID, diag.Scorecard.Score, *minScore, diag.Scorecard.Grade)
144			} else {
145				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: bundle %q failed strict validation (%d errors, %d broken links); installation rolled back\n",
146					manifest.ID, len(diag.Errors), len(diag.BrokenLinks))
147			}
148			exitFunc(1)
149			return
150		}
151	
152		if err := staging.Commit(".", manifest.ID); err != nil {
153			rollback()
154			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: bundle %q could not be installed: %v (installation rolled back)\n", manifest.ID, err)
155			exitFunc(1)
156			return
157		}
158	
159		lockPath := "okf.lock"
160		lf, err := lock.ReadLockfile(lockPath)
161		if err != nil {
162			lf = &lock.Lockfile{Version: 1}
163		}
164		lf.Upsert(lock.BundleEntry{
165			ID:          manifest.ID,
166			Source:      target,
167			Version:     manifest.Version,
168			Hash:        manifest.Hash,
169			InstalledAt: time.Now().UTC(),
170		})
171		if err := lock.WriteLockfile(lockPath, lf); err != nil {
172			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to update okf.lock: %v\n", err)
173		}
174	
175		if diag.Scorecard != nil {
176			fmt.Printf("Bundle quality score: %d/100 (Grade: %s)\n", diag.Scorecard.Score, diag.Scorecard.Grade)
177		}
178		fmt.Printf("Successfully installed and verified %s in %s\n", manifest.ID, vendorDisplay)
179	}

58	func runRestore(registryURL string, force bool, minScores ...int) {

76		client := newRegistryClient(registryURL)
77		restoredCount := 0
78		skippedCount := 0

80		for _, entry := range lf.Bundles {
81			// okf.lock may come from a repository: its ids must resolve inside

101			}

104			}
105	
106			fmt.Printf("Resolving %s from %s...\n", entry.ID, client.BaseURL)

113	
114			if entry.Hash != "" {

132			}

138			}
139	
140			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(staging.Dir, "index.md")); os.IsNotExist(err) {
141				rollback()
142				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: bundle %q is not a valid OKF v0.2 bundle: missing index.md (installation rolled back)\n", manifest.ID)
143				exitFunc(1)

# Automated Security Auditing & Defensive Verification Workflow

## Context & Objectives

To maintain the highest level of defensive assurance for `okf-agent-memory`, automated security auditing is integrated into the local and CI verification pipeline (`make security-audit` and `make check`), complemented by adversarial agent security reviews and regression testing against `docs/security/SECURITY_AUDIT.md`.

---

## 1. Automated Static & Vulnerability Analysis (`make security-audit`)

Every verification run executes static security analysis and vulnerability scanning across all Go packages:

```bash
make security-audit
```

* **`gosec`**: Inspects Go AST for security weaknesses (`-exclude=G301,G306 -exclude-dir=examples ./...`). Every intentional file access in `pkg/okf`, `pkg/sync`, `pkg/vault`, and `pkg/registry` must first pass canonical boundary containment (`ensureWithinRoot` or `validateTreePath`) before `#nosec` annotations are permitted.

10	## Context & Problem Statement
11	
12	OKF Agent Memory is designed to be written, updated, and queried by autonomous AI agents operating across IDEs and CI/CD pipelines. Because AI agent tool calls may execute untrusted or adversarial prompts, the deterministic tooling layer must treat all mutation arguments and bundle directories as untrusted inputs.
13	
14	## Security Controls & Defense-in-Depth
15	
16	The tooling layer enforces defensive confinement across eight critical choke-points:
17	
18	### 1. Canonical Bundle Confinement (`ensureWithinRoot`)
19	All file reads in `LoadBundle` and writes in `SaveConcept`, `UpdateParentIndex`, and `AppendLogEntry` resolve symlinks and compare canonical paths against the bundle root via `filepath.Rel`.
20	- Traversal via relative parent references (`..`) or absolute paths escaping the bundle directory is strictly denied.
21	- The bundle root is absolutised **before** its symlinks are resolved. A relative root under a symlinked working directory (macOS `/tmp` → `/private/tmp`) otherwise stayed unresolved while the target resolved to the real path, and every legitimate write was refused as an escape.
22	- Root-reserved files (`index.md`, `log.md`, `AGENTS.md`) cannot be overwritten as arbitrary concept documents regardless of letter case (`strings.EqualFold`). Subdirectory concepts (e.g. `architecture/agents.md`) remain permissible.
23	
24	### 2. Symlink Escape Prevention
25	To defend against Local File Inclusion (LFI) and Arbitrary File Overwrite:
26	- `LoadBundle` inspects symlinks with `ensureWithinRoot`. Any symlink whose resolved target escapes the canonical bundle root triggers an immediate traversal error.
27	- Symlinks must point strictly to markdown (`.md`) files within the bundle; symlinks to directories or non-markdown assets are rejected.
28	- Writing through symlinks pointing outside the bundle is blocked.
29	
30	#### Symlinked bundle roots
31	The bundle root itself may be a symlink, because users legitimately link a bundle into place. The target is confined by scope:
32	- **Project and vendor bundles** (`LoadBundle`): the root symlink must resolve inside the directory that contains the link. A repository that ships `knowledge -> /elsewhere` is therefore rejected, with or without a trailing slash.
33	- **User and system scope roots** (`~/.okf`, `/etc/okf`, `OKF_USER_DIR`, `OKF_SYSTEM_DIR`; internal `loadTrustedBundle`): the root is configured by the user, not by the repository, so it may be a symlink to any location. Symlinks inside these bundles stay confined by rule 2.
34	- A `knowledge/` subdirectory symlink is always confined to its parent root, including in trusted scopes.
35	- The walk always runs over the resolved root. Walking the unresolved path loaded an empty bundle silently, because `filepath.WalkDir` does not follow a symlink at its root.
36	
37	### 3. Frontmatter & Metadata Injection Defense (`sanitizeConceptMetadata`)
38	Metadata fields (`type`, `title`, `description`, `actor`) are strictly validated prior to serialization:
39	- Newline characters (`\r`, `\n`) are rejected in scalar metadata fields, preventing YAML attribute smuggling or forged verification states (`verified.by: human`).
40	- The YAML document delimiter (`---`) is forbidden within metadata values.
41	- Special scalar characters (`:`, `&`, `"`, etc.) are quoted safely in YAML serialization without escaping HTML entities.
42	
43	### 4. MCP Server Root Confinement (`resolveBundleDir`)
44	The stdio Model Context Protocol (MCP) server confines dynamic bundle switching:
45	- The server initializes with a canonical `rootDir` (governed by project workspace or `OKF_MCP_ROOT`).
46	- When `OKF_MCP_ROOT` is unset, the root is derived from the bundle's parent. If a multi-segment relative path is given (e.g. `docs/knowledge`), the bundle path is normalized to absolute first to prevent double-joining while maintaining strict boundary confinement.
47	- Multi-bundle projects can dynamically select sub-bundles (e.g. `bundle="examples/software"`), but any request escaping the server root is denied before loading.
48	- Required MCP mutation arguments (`concept_id`, `type`, `title`, `description`) are strictly non-empty.
49	
50	### 5. Collaborative File Permissions (`0o644` / `0o755`)
51	OKF bundles are designed for shared Git repository version control:
52	- Files are created with `0o644` (rw-r--r--) and directories with `0o755` (rwxr-xr-x).
53	- Static analysis rules intended for secret credential files (such as `gosec G301/G306` requiring `0600`/`0750`) are deliberately excluded, ensuring bundle readability across multi-user environments, CI/CD runners, and Git sub-processes.
54	
55	### 6. Human Verification Provenance (`ensureNoForgedHumanVerification`)
56	`SaveConcept` refuses to let a non-human actor add a human verification:
57	- A human identity is `human`, `human:*`, or `human/*`, compared case-insensitively (`IsHumanIdentity`). The `verified.by=human` filter uses the same definition, so the guard and the filter cannot disagree.
58	- An agent may preserve `verified` entries already recorded in the concept file. Adding one, or altering the timestamp of an existing one, is rejected. A new concept inherits nothing from an existing file at its path.
59	- Scope of the guarantee: the actor is self-declared. The MCP server fixes it to `agent/mcp`, so the guard is effective there. A CLI user can still pass `--actor human/...`, so for the CLI it guards against accidental or injected forgery, not against a deliberate caller.
60	
61	### 7. Remote Input Write Containment (Hub Sync and Registry Installs)
62	Hub tree manifests, registry manifests, registry archives, and `okf.lock` entries are untrusted input: any holder of the vault key, a compromised registry, or a cloned repository controls them. Every path built from them must land inside the target bundle or workspace before anything is written or deleted.
63	- **Hub tree paths** (`pkg/sync`, `validateTreePath`): a path that is empty, absolute or volume-qualified, contains `.`, `..` or empty segments, contains a hidden segment, a NUL byte, or a backslash separator is refused before any blob is fetched. Every write and delete target is then resolved through symlinks and must lie strictly inside the resolved bundle root (`filepath.Rel`, not a string prefix). One bad entry refuses the whole `okf hub pull` or `okf hub sync`, and a stored sync state that holds such a path is ignored.
64	- **Sync state**: `.okf/sync-state.json` is read and written only when it resolves inside the bundle.
65	- **Registry bundle ids** (`pkg/registry`, `ValidateBundleID`): an id must be a canonical relative slash path. Registry manifests and `okf.lock` entries with an absolute, `..`, `.`, empty, backslash, or NUL id are refused with an error naming the manifest or entry. Scoped and nested ids (`@peter/django-5-rules`, `acme/tools/linter`) remain valid. `.okf/vendor` must resolve inside the workspace, and each bundle directory strictly inside `.okf/vendor` (`ResolveVendorDir`).
66	- **Archive extraction**: every entry is checked lexically and through symlinks before anything is extracted, so an archive is applied in full or not at all.
67	- **Staged installs and rollback**: `okf pull` and `okf restore` extract and validate in a fresh staging directory under `.okf`, then move it into place. A failed install discards only that staging directory. Rollback never removes a directory this invocation did not create, and never follows a symlink. `okf vendor remove` re-resolves its target and unlinks a symlink instead of following it.
68	
69	### 8. Concurrent Local Write Serialization & Optimistic Concurrency Control (`WithBundleLock`)
70	To prevent silent Read-Modify-Write (RMW) lost updates when parallel subagents, multiple IDE MCP servers, or concurrent CLI invocations mutate the same local bundle (`knowledge/` or `~/.okf/`):
71	- **Stage 1 (Cross-Process Bundle Write Lock)**: `InitBundle`, `SaveConcept`, `UpdateConcept`, `RelateConcepts`, `UpdateParentIndex`, and `AppendLogEntry` acquire an exclusive lockfile (`.okf-write.lock`, confined via `ensureWithinRoot` and created atomically with `os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL`) across the entire mutation transaction (concept write + parent `index.md` update + `log.md` bookkeeping), with bounded backoff and automatic stale-lock eviction (`acquired_at` age check).
72	- **Stage 2a (Transactional RMW Scope)**: `UpdateConcept` (used by `okf update` and MCP `okf_update`) and `RelateConcepts` (`okf relate` and MCP `okf_relate`) acquire the bundle lock **before** calling `LoadBundle`, ensuring concurrent updates or link insertions on the same concept execute strictly in sequence against the latest committed disk state.
73	- **Stage 2b (Optimistic Concurrency Check / CAS)**: `LoadBundle` records the SHA-256 digest (`sourceHash`) of each loaded concept file. When `SaveConcept` writes an existing concept (`IsNew: false`) that was loaded via `LoadBundle` outside `UpdateConcept`, it verifies inside the bundle lock that the on-disk file still matches `sourceHash`, returning `ErrConcurrentModification` if another writer modified the file in the interim.
74	
75	## Relationships

78	- Complements the deterministic single-binary tooling in [tooling-decision](tooling-decision.md).
